# Apply for an Aadhaar Card Online And Offline – How To Check Application Status

23 December 2022

![Apply for aadhaar card](https://navi.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/guide-to-apply-for-aadhar-card.jpg)

Aadhaar Card was introduced by the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) in 2010 to provide a unique identification number (UIN) to every Indian citizen. Many benefits such as government schemes, pensions and LPG subsidies can be availed with the Aadhaar card. Applying for an Aadhaar card is simple and easy. Read on to know the process.

> **Latest Update**
>
> UIDAI recently announced that people, whose Aadhaar cards were issued more than 10 years ago, can update their demographic details on myAadhaar portal for FREE from 15th March, 2023 to 30th June, 2023.

## **How to Apply for an Aadhaar Card Online?**

You can follow the following steps to get an Aadhaar card online:

1. ****Step 1: Visit UIDAI Website****

   First, visit the [official website](https://uidai.gov.in/en/) of the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI).![](https://navi.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/guide-to-apply-for-aadhar-card-step-1.jpg)
2. ****Step 2: Select Get Aadhaar****

   Under the ‘My Aadhaar’ section, browse to the subsection ‘Get Aadhaar’. Below that, click on ‘Locate an Enrollment Centre’.![](https://navi.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/guide-to-apply-for-aadhar-card-step-2.jpg)
3. ****Step 3:** **Select State or Postal Code****

   A new page will open displaying the three options – State, Postal (PIN) Code and Search Box. Click on any of the three options and input the relevant data.![](https://navi.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/guide-to-apply-for-aadhar-card-step-3.png)
4. ****Step 4: Fill out the Form****

   You will be displayed a form on the screen. Fill it up, enter the captcha verification code and select a centre close to your residence![](https://navi.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/guide-to-apply-for-aadhar-card-step-4.png)
5. ****Step 5:** **Visit Centre with Supporting Documents****

   On the day of your appointment, visit the centre with all the supporting documents that include proof of identity, date of birth proof, address proof and proof of relationship with the head of the family
6. ****Step 6: Fulfil the Formalities****

   Fill up the enrollment form and submit all the relevant documents. Provide all the biometric information such as fingerprint and iris scan that the Aadhaar official asks for.
7. ****Step 7: Collect Acknowledgement Slip****

   After submitting the enrollment form, collect your acknowledgement slip. You can track your application status by using the URN number printed on the slip.

## **How To Apply for an Aadhaar Card Offline?**

### **1. Locate an Aadhaar Enrollment Centre Online**

UIDAI (Unique Identification Authority of India) has authorised different entities to collect biometric and demographic data for the enrollment process. You can go to either an Aadhaar Enrollment Centre/Aadhaar camp or a Permanent Enrollment Centre to apply for an Aadhaar card.

To locate an Aadhaar Enrollment Centre near your location, follow these steps:

1. Visit [UIDAI’s official website](https://uidai.gov.in/en/), over on ‘My Aadhaar’ section and click on ‘Locate an Enrollment Centre.
2. Select State or Postal Code
3. Enter the Captcha code and click ‘Locate a Centre’. The list of Aadhaar centres would be displayed.

### **2. Download Form**

1. Visit [UIDAI’s official website](https://uidai.gov.in/en/), over on ‘Aadhaar Enrolment/Update Form’
2. Take a printout of Form
3. Fill out the Form completely

### **3. Visit the Centre with Supporting Documents**

You will need to carry several documents as proof of identity and age to enrol for an Aadhaar card. Make sure to carry the original documents and photocopies to the enrollment centre.

The following is a list of documents required to apply for a new Aadhaar card.

* **Identity Proof**: Voter ID card, [PAN card](https://navi.com/blog/pan-card-in-india/), passport, driving license, ration card, pensioner photo card, disability ID card, CGHS/ECHS card, ST/SC/OBC certificate with a photograph.
* **Address Proof**: Water/electricity/telephone/gas bill, PAN card, passport, bank statement, passbook, driving license, Voter ID card, property tax receipt and [credit card](https://navi.com/blog/what-is-credit-card/) statement.
* **Age Proof**: Birth certificate, PAN card, government board/university issued mark sheet, SSLC book/certificate.
* **Proof of Relationship Documents**: Marriage certificate, pension card, MNREGA job card, CGHS/ECHS/[ESIC](https://navi.com/blog/employee-state-insurance-corporation-scheme/) card, PDS card, any government family entitlement document, certificate of identity issued by village panchayat head.

### **4. Process of Aadhaar Card Enrollment**

Once you have all the required documents, follow these steps to enrol for an Aadhaar card:

1. At the centre, the officials would record your biometric information such as fingerprints & iris scan.
2. For children below the age of five, a parent/guardian has to submit their name, Aadhaar and biometrics information.
3. Collect the acknowledgment slip that contains the 14-digit Aadhaar enrollment number that you can use to track your application.

## **How to Check the Status of Your Aadhaar Card Enrollment Online?**

After you have received the acknowledgement slip, there is a turnaround time of 90 days for the Aadhaar generation. If you want to check the status of your application within this time, follow these steps:

1. Check the Enrollment ID in the mentioned slip. This is a 28-digit number with a 14-digit enrollment number and a 14-digit date and time stamp. You will need only the first 14 numbers to check the application status.

1. Go to [UIDAI’s website](https://uidai.gov.in/en/) and click on ‘Check Aadhaar Status’ from the ‘My Aadhaar’ menu.

1. Click on ‘Check Enrollment and Update Status’.

1. Enter the Enrollment ID and security captcha.

You can make corrections in the enrollment data within 96 hours or 4 days of applying for the new Aadhaar card. If you cannot do them within this period, you will have to wait till your Aadhaar card gets generated.

## **Steps to Make Corrections in the Information Provided During Enrollment**

You can correct and update any demographic details on your Aadhaar card at any time and from anywhere by visiting the official website of UIDAI. Changing your mobile number is also possible online using the Indian Postal Service website.

You can follow these steps to correct/update/change the details on your Aadhaar card:

**Step 1:** Visit the [myAadhaar Self-Service Update Portal](https://ssup.uidai.gov.in/ssup/login.html).

**Step 2:** Click on the login option.

**Step 3:** Enter your 12-digit Aadhaar number, the captcha and click on “Send OTP”.

**Step 4:** Enter the [OTP](https://navi.com/blog/one-time-password/) that you receive on the mobile number registered in UIDAI’s database and log in to your Aadhaar account.

**Step 5:** Under the “Services” section, click on the “Update Aadhaar Online” option to correct any details like name, date of birth, gender, language and address as mentioned on your Aadhaar card.

**Step 6:** On the next page, click on the option “Proceed to Update Aadhaar”.

**Step 7:** Choose the details you want to correct or update and click on the “Proceed to Update Aadhaar”. Keep in mind that there is a limit on the number of times you can correct your details.

**Step 8:** You can now view the details as they are present on the Aadhaar Card and can do the necessary corrections and upload the scanned copies of the supporting documents.

**Step 9:** Check the preview of the corrected details and pay the online update fee of Rs. 50 (non-refundable) by using either your debit or credit card or via [net banking](https://navi.com/blog/what-is-net-banking/).

**Step 10:** After payment, an Update Request Number (URN) will be generated that can be used to check the status of the Aadhaar update request.  
This process takes around 90 days, after which you can download the updated Aadhaar card and take a printout of it.

## **How to Change Mobile Number, E-mail or Biometric Data on Aadhaar?**

If you wish to change any biometric data, email id or mobile number offline, you can visit your nearest Aadhaar Seva Kendra. Mentioned below are the steps that will help you with the process:

* **Step 1:** Fill up the [Aadhaar correction form](https://navi.com/blog/aadhaar-correction-and-enrollment-form/) with all the correct information.
* **Step 2:** Submit all the supporting documents for validating your correction request along with the correction form.
* **Step 3:** Pay the fee that is required for correcting the details.

Please note that the fee for correction or updation is fixed to Rs.100 if it includes updating biometrics and Rs. 50 if only demographic details are updated.

## **How to Check Aadhaar Card Enrollment Status via SMS?**

Here are the steps to check Aadhaar card enrollment status via SMS:

1. Go to create new SMS on your phone and type “UID STATUS <14 DIGIT ENROLLMENT NUMBER>”.
2. Send the SMS to 51969.
3. If an Aadhaar number has been generated, you will receive an SMS containing the Aadhaar number.
4. If an Aadhaar number has not been generated, an SMS will be sent specifying the current status of your Aadhaar card.

## **How to Download the E-Aadhaar Card Online?**

After around 15 working days of enrollment, your Aadhaar application will be processed, and you will receive an update on your registered mobile number. This is when you can download a soft copy of the Aadhaar card called the E-Aadhaar card.

It is a digital and password-protected copy of your Aadhaar, which can be used for verification purposes. To download the E-Aadhaar copy online, follow these steps:

1. Go to [UIDAI’s official website](https://uidai.gov.in/en/), hover the cursor over ‘My Aadhaar’ and select ‘Download Aadhaar’
2. Select any of the given options- Enrollment ID, Aadhaar number or Virtual number
3. Enter the 28-digit enrollment ID, 16-digit virtual ID or 12-digit Aadhaar number and security code.
4. Click on ‘Send OTP’ and enter the One Time Password you have received on your mobile number.
5. Click on ‘Validate and Download’ to get a copy of your e-Aadhaar card. It will be a password-protected PDF file, with the password being the first four letters of your name and birth year in YYYY format.

## **How to Reprint an Aadhaar Card?**

Here are the steps to apply for an Aadhaar card reprint online, using the UIDAI portal:

1. Visit the [UIDAI website](https://uidai.gov.in/en/) and click on the “Order Aadhaar Reprint” option under the get Aadhaar section.
2. Select either Aadhaar number (UID), enrollment ID (EID) or virtual ID (VID) and proceed.
3. Make online payment of Rs.50, using either debit card, Credit card, net banking or Unified Payment Interface (UPI).
4. Save the acknowledgement slip that is generated.
5. UIDAI will dispatch the Aadhaar card to the registered address within 5 working days via speed post.

## **Final Word**

These days having an Aadhaar card is a necessity as the government requires it when availing of various services/benefits. Fortunately, the process to apply for an Aadhaar card is easy as you can get it done from any authorized enrollment Centre in India.

## **FAQs**

**Q1. **Can I make corrections to the details of my Aadhaar card?****

Ans: Yes, you can make corrections both during and after the enrollment process. If you fail to submit corrections within the first 4 days, you will have to wait till the new card is issued. However, make sure that you have submitted a valid phone number as it will allow you to make corrections online.

**Q2. **Who can apply for an Aadhaar card?****

Ans: Any Indian citizen residing in the country, regardless of age or gender, can apply for an Aadhaar card. As long as you have stayed here for 182 days or more, you can apply for it. NRIs and foreigners can also apply if they fulfil this condition.

**Q3. **How can I update my residential address on the Aadhaar card?****

Ans: You can update your residential address online via the official portal of UIDAI, provided that you have a registered and valid mobile number. To do so, log in with your Aadhaar Number, make a data update request and upload the necessary documents.

**Q4. **What is the Aadhaar enrollment procedure for children?****

Ans: You can enrol children below five years of age, including infants, for the blue coloured Aadhaar card, called [Baal Aadhaar card](https://navi.com/blog/baal-aadhaar-card/). When they become older than five years, you need to update their biometric details to keep the card valid.  Once they reach 15 years, you will need to update the biometric details again.

**Q5. **How can I lock the details of my E-Aadhaar card to prevent its misuse?****

Ans: Follow the given steps to lock your E-Aadhaar card:  
**Step 1**: Visit the official website of [UIDAI](https://uidai.gov.in/en/).  
**Step 2**: Enter your UID or VID, followed by the security code.  
**Step 3**: Enter the OTP received on your mobile number.  
**Step 4**: Pick a password for your Aadhaar card and click on ‘Enable’.

# Aadhaar Data Update

An Aadhaar Data Update form can be used when an Indian resident wants to update any of the details in his/her Aadhaar card. The details captured on the Aadhaar card of every resident are recorded in the UIDAI system. It is necessary for the Aadhaar cardholders to keep their details updated whenever there are biometric or demographic changes as they get saved in the Central Identities Data Repository (CIDR). In this article, we look at the process for updating Aadhar card details. To know more about

[Linking Aadhaar with UAN - EPFO](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/linking-aadhaar-with-uan-epfo)

## Aadhaar Card Details Update

The UIDAI (Unique Identification Authority of India) enables the Aadhaar card holders to correct or update their demographic details on the authority’s database. The biometric data can only be updated at an enrolment centre.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Demographic information** | **Biometric information** |
| Name, Address, Date of Birth/Age, e-mail Address, Gender, Mobile Number, Relationship Status and Information Sharing Consent. | Iris, Finger Prints and Facial Photograph. |

## Required Documents

The following documents are accepted by the UIDAI for the purpose of verifying, updating or correcting information in the Aadhaar Card.

* **Proof of Identification:-** An identity documents that includes Ration/PDS Photo Card, PAN Card, Passport, Driving license, etc.
* **Proof of Address:-**The address proof documents that include Bank Account details/Passbook, Electricity bill, water bill and telephone, Property Tax receipt, Credit Card statement, etc.
* **Proof of Date of Birth:-**The documents accepted for the proof of identity that includes Birth Certificate, Mark sheet issued by any Government Board or University, PAN card, etc.

## Aadhar Data Update Charges

Method of updating or correcting Aadhar details through online and via post can be done free of cost. If done at the enrollment centre for the correction/update, the applicant will be charged a fee of Rs. 25/-.

## Turnaround Time

The processing time for the updates or corrections in the Aadhar card will take 7-10 days after the request.

## Methods for Updating Aadhaar Card Details

The residents can update or correct their Aadhar card details via 3 modes:

1. Update Data Online
2. Update Data via Post
3. Visiting nearby Enrolment Centre

These are the modes where residents place their demographic/biometric update request.

## Update Data Online

The applicants have to follow the given steps to update or make corrections to the Aadhar card by submitting their request online.

### Access Self Service Update Portal (SSUP)

**Step 1:**

Applicants has to visit the official site of Aadhar Self Service Update Portal (SSUP) to update or correct their Aadhar details from the portal.

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/aa-1-2.jpg)

Step 1 - Aadhaar Data Update

### Login to the portal

**Step 2:**

Using Aadhaar number or registered mobile number of the resident are required to log in to the portal. After that, enter the Text Verification and click on the "Send OTP" option.

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/aa-2.jpg)

Step 2 - Aadhaar Data Update

**Step 3:**

Enter the OTP with the Captcha code and click on “Submit” option.

### Aadhar Data Update Request

**Step 4:**

After submitting, it will get directed to a new page which is “Data Request Page”. Now you need to select the field where the changes must be done.

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/aa-3.jpg)

Step 4 - Aadhar Data Update

### Upload Requested Documents

**Step 5:**

Then you have to attach the specified documents in the portal. Ensure to scan (with a colour scanner) and upload the proof of the changed details that has been updated.

**Step 6:**

The documents will be verified against the requested data by a Verifier of UIDAI’s Update back-office.

### Provide Details

**Step 7:**

Then you have to fill out the data in the selected fields.

**Step 8:**

After filling the details and double check on the accuracy of the information as it will get reflected in the new Aadhaar card.

### Download Update Request Number (URN) receipt

**Step 9:**

A URN (Update Request Number) will be generated through which the Aadhaar card update process can be tracked or verified by the applicant.

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/aa-5.jpg)

Step 9 - Aadhaar Data Update

**Step 10:**

You can drop the receipt or download a copy containing the URN. Once updated, you can download the updated Aadhar card and print it. The updated Aadhaar card will be mailed to the registered address.

## Updating Aadhar Details via Post

The applicants can also send a request via post to update or make corrections in their Aadhar card. The applicant has to follow the given steps to complete the process.

### Download Application Form

**Step 1:**

You have to download the application form for the Aadhar data correction/update process. The application form is reproduced below for your ready references:

***[Open PDF in new tab](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/Aadhaar-Data-Update-Form-03-1.pdf)***

### Fill the Required Details

**Step 2:**

You have to fill the required details which you want to change in your Aadhaar card.

### Attach Documents

**Step 3:**

You will have to submit the photocopies of the documents that validate the changes requested to be made in the form.

### Dispatch the Application

**Step 4:**

Send the form along with the documents to any one of the postal address as mentioned below:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Address 1** | **Address 2** |
| UIDAI Post Box No. 10, Chhindwara, Madhya Pradesh – 480001, India. | Post Box No. 99, Banjara Hills, Hyderabad – 500034, India. |

## Visiting Nearby Enrolment Centre

Aadhaar Enrolment centres that enrol the applicants for Aadhaar after taking their biometric and demographic details following the UIDAI enrolment process. Aadhaar Enrolment Centres in other cities can be found on Aadhaar Enrolment Centres link, which will take you to the below-displayed screen: The Aadhar card holders can update their details by visiting the nearest Enrolment Centre by following the steps specified below:

![Content image](https://img.indiafilings.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/aa-23.jpg)

Enrollment centre - Aadhaar Data Update

### Get Application Form

**Step 1:**

Aadhaar Data Update form has to be filled by the applicant.

**Step 2:**

Ensure to give the correct details in the application form.

### Provide self-attested proofs

**Step 3:**

You have to provide the self-attested proofs to support the changes as per your request.

**Step 4:**

After that, submit the form and the relevant document proofs to the Executive in the centre.

### End of Process

**Step 5:**

The Enrolment Centres will charge Rs. 25/- for every such visit towards the correction of details like biometric data or Demographic information such as mobile numbers, address, photo etc.

**Note:**

Children those who are of 5 years old must visit the Aadhaar enrolment centre to submit their biometric data. After 15 years of age, they must revisit an enrolment centre to provide their biometric data. This biometric data is considered as the final one which remains with your Aadhaar for a lifetime.

## Track/Check Application Status

You can also track/verify your application status online via Self Service Update Portal (SSUP). Provide your Aadhar number; URN number received SRN number along with the text verification. Then you have to click on the get status button. The status of your Aadhar data update will be displayed on the screen.

Digital transformation has revolutionized various aspects of our lives, and the application process for an Aadhaar card is no exception. No more standing in long queues or dealing with cumbersome paperwork – now you can acquire this essential identification document with just a few clicks.

## Understanding the Aadhaar Card

You are eager to understand **how to apply for Aadhaar Card online**. But let’s begin with a quick overview of what an Aadhaar card is and why it’s essential. The Aadhaar card is a 12-digit identification number, given by the [UIDAI](https://www.indiainfoline.com/knowledge-center/kyc/what-is-uid) (Unique Identification Authority of India). That’s a document of identification and address for Indian citizens. You can easily avail various government schemes, subsidies, and services with an Aadhaar.

## Eligibility Criteria to Apply for Aadhaar Card Online

To begin the new Aadhaar card application process, certain basic eligibility conditions must be met, which are:

* The applicant should be an Indian Citizen
* The applicant should have valid documents to provide for identity, address, and date of birth verification.
* The applicant’s mobile number and email ID should be active.
* For NRIs (Non-Resident Indians), the applicant must have spent more than 182 days in India, and they should have a valid Indian Passport

* A valid proof of identification, such as a Valid PAN card, Voter ID Card or a Passport.

* Date of Birth Certificate

## How do I apply for Aadhaar Card Online?

In order to **apply online for Aadhaar card**, follow these simple steps:

### Step 1: Visit the UIDAI site

Begin by visiting the official Aadhaar website. Just type “uidai. gov.in” in your browser and press Enter. This is the government portal where all of the Aadhaar services are present under one roof.

### Step 2: Look for the Aadhaar Application Option

Once the home page opens, just scroll down to search for the Aadhaar enrolment section. There will be a link that reads something like “Apply for Aadhaar” or “Get New Aadhaar.” So just click on the one you prefer.

Now, you’ll be taken to a page where you’ll have to complete a form with general information about yourself — name, date of birth, address and other relevant information. This is important, so don’t rush here. Double-check before proceeding.

### Step 4: Select an Enrolment Centre

When you are done with the form, you will be required to choose an enrolment centre near you. Use your area PIN code to search for a centre near you to avail of services at your ease.

### 5: Set Up an Appointment

### Step 6: Go to the Centre with Documents

On the day of the appointment, bring the necessary documents — proof of identity and address. An official will check your papers and capture biometric data, including fingerprints and an iris scan.

### Step 7: Preserve the Acknowledgement Slip Carefully

After the enrollment, you will be given a slip with an enrollment number. This number enables you to check the status of your Aadhaar application online.

results.title: Documents Required for Aadhar Card Enrolment and Update
results.content:
Updated: 18-02-2026 12:23:14 PM

You have to visit an Aadhaar Enrolment Centre or an Aadhar Sewa Kendra to enrol for a new Aadhaar card. You are asked to provide your demographic and biometric details at the time of enrolment. Apart from these details, you need to submit the document proof that verifies your details mentioned in the Aadhaar Enrolment Form. [...] Certificate of birth
 SSLC Book/ Certificate
 Passport of the applicant
 PAN Card
 Certificate of Date of Birth which is issued by Group A Gazetted Officer on letterhead
 A certificate or ID Card having photo and DOB duly signed and issued by a Government authority
 Photo ID card having DOB, issued by recognized Educational Institution
 Marksheet which has been issued by any Government Board or University
 Government Photo Id Card or Photo Identity Proof or PSU issued ID card which contains DoB
 Pension Payment Order (Central or State)
 Central Government Health Service Scheme Photo Card or Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme Photo Identity card
 School Leaving Certificate (SLC)/ School Transfer Certificate (TC) having name and DOB [...] Proof of residence
 Proof of identity
 Birth certificate
 Aadhaar of any one of the parents

The documents accepted as Identity proof are given below:

 Passport Copy
 PAN Card Copy
 Voter ID Copy
 Driving License

The documents accepted as Address proof are given below:

 Passport Copy of Spouse
 A Copy of Ration Card
 Voter ID Card
 Driving License
 Credit Card Statement (last 3 months)
 Bank Statement Or Passbook
 Electricity Bill (Last 3 months)
 Water bill (Last 3 months)
 Gas Connection Bill (Last 3 months)
 Landline Phone Bill (Last 3 months)
 Insurance Policy

# Documents Required for Aadhar Card Enrolment and Update

[Home](https://www.paisabazaar.com/) [Aadhaar Card](https://www.paisabazaar.com/aadhar-card/) Documents Required for Aadhar Card

An Aadhaar Card is a 12-digit unique identification number issued by the UIDAI on behalf of the government to every resident of India. This page covers list of Aadhar card documents required for Aadhaar Card correction, Aadhaar Card update, and address update as well.

Updated: 18-02-2026 12:23:14 PM

You have to visit an Aadhaar Enrolment Centre or an Aadhar Sewa Kendra to enrol for a new Aadhaar card. You are asked to provide your demographic and biometric details at the time of enrolment. Apart from these details, you need to submit the document proof that verifies your details mentioned in the Aadhaar Enrolment Form.

[![](https://www.paisabazaar.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Image-6-300x300.webp)](https://leap.axis.bank.in/verification?query=5ee36547c0ce0dd6c0a2812d&utm_campaign=dbg_paisabazaar&utm_content=0c782247-31e9-408f-9d18-e3f365ca6658&utm_medium=cpc&utm_source=PB)  
 There are various documents required for Aadhaar card for resident Indians and these would be required even while making any correction in the Aadhaar card later. It is recommended to carry all original document proof at the time of Aadhaar enrolment or [Aadhaar update](https://www.paisabazaar.com/aadhar-card/aadhaar-card-update-correction/).

**Table of Contents :**

**Find List of Documents Required for Aadhaar Card for Resident Indians**

* 1. [List of Identity Proofs](#identity)
  2. [List of Address Proofs](#address)
  3. [List of Date of Birth Proofs](#birth)
  4. [Proofs of Relationship](#proof)
* [Documents Required for Aadhaar Card for Child/Minors](#child)
* [Documents Required for OCI Cardholders/LTV Document Holders/Nepal & Bhutan Nationals and Other Resident Foreigners](#foreigners)
* [FAQs](#faq)

## **List of Identity Proofs – Documents Required for New Aadhaar Card**

You can submit any of the following supporting documents acceptable by [UIDAI](https://www.paisabazaar.com/aadhar-card/uidai/) as Identity proof:

* Passport
* [PAN card](https://www.paisabazaar.com/pan-card/)
* Ration or PDS Photo card
* Voter Identification card
* Driving licence of the applicant
* Photo identification cards issued by the Government of India/ Service photo ID cards that are issued by a PSU
* Job card of MG-NREGS
* Photo identification that is issued by a Recognised Educational Institution
* Licence of Arms
* Photo Bank ATM card
* Photo Credit card
* Photo card of the Pensioner
* Photo card of the Freedom Fighter
* Photo Passbook of Kisan
* Photo card of CGHS/ECHS
* Certificate of Marriage
* A document containing proof of the marriage of the applicant issued originally by the marriage Registrar (which is mandatory to submit after marriage)
* Legally approved name change certificate
* Residing Address card of the applicant that contains both the name and the photo that was originally issued by the Department of Posts
* Identity Certificate containing the photo of the applicant on a proper letterhead issued by either a Gazetted Officer or a Tehsildar
* Either a handicapped medical certificate or a disability Identification card that is issued by either the State Government, the UT Government, or any such Administration
* Bhamashah Card/Jan-Aadhaar card issued by Govt. of  
   Rajasthan
* Certificate from Warden/Superintendent/Matron/Head of Institution of recognized shelter homes or orphanages, etc.
* Certificate of Identity having photo issued by MP/MLA/MLC/Municipal Councilor or Village Panchayat Head/ Mukhiya or its equivalent authority (for rural areas)
* Gazette notification for name change
* RSBY Card
* SSLC book having applicant’s photograph
* ST/SC/OBC certificate with photo
* School Leaving Certificate (SLC)/ School Transfer Certificate (TC) containing name and photograph
* Passbook of the bank Pass having name and photograph
* Extract of school records issued by Head of School containing name and photograph
* Certificate of Identity having name and photo issued by Recognized Educational Institution and signed by Head of Institute
* Certificate of identity containing name, date of birth and photograph issued by EPFO

## **List of Address Proofs – Documents Required for Aadhar Card Registration**

Documents that contain the proof of residing address of the applicant are one of the most important documents to be submitted to the authorized Aadhaar centre. These documents must be proper because the [Aadhar card](https://www.paisabazaar.com/aadhar-card/) is sent to the address specified by the applicant in the form. If the applicant fails to present the correct address proof or update the same, he may [not receive the Aadhaar card](https://www.paisabazaar.com/aadhar-card/aadhaar-card-not-received/). The following documents are accepted by the UIDAI as address proof for Aadhaar registration:

* Passport
* Passbook or Bank Statement
* Account statement or passbook of the Post Office
* Ration Card
* Voter Identification card
* Driving licence of the applicant
* Photo identification cards issued by the Government
* PSU issued a Service photo ID card with the address
* Previous 3 months’ electricity bill
* Water bill as long as it is not more than 3 months’ old
* Previous three months’ landline bill related to telephone
* Receipt showing the Property Tax of the last 3 months
* Last three months’ Credit Card statement
* Insurance policy
* Photo and a letter with an address signed by the bank on letterhead
* Signed letter with address and photo on the letterhead of the company issued by the registered office
* Photo and signed letter with address issued by a well-known educational enterprise on their letterhead
* Job card of NREGS
* Arms license
* Pensioner card
* Freedom fighter card
* Kisan passbook
* CGHS/ECHS card
* Address certificate along with a photo on their letterhead that is issued either by an MP, MLA, Gazetted Officer or Tehsildar
* Address Certificate issued by the Village Panchayat head or any authority equivalent to them for rural areas
* Assessment order of the [Income Tax](https://www.paisabazaar.com/tax/e-filing-of-income-tax/)
* Registration certificate of the vehicle
* Registered agreement for sale, lease, or rent of the applicant’s residential address.
* Photo and address card by the Department of Posts
* Caste and Domicile certificate along with a photo that the State Government has issued
* Previous 3 month bill of gas connection
* Either a handicapped medical certificate or a disability Identification card that is issued by either a State Government, UT Government or any Administrations
* Spouse’s or partner’s passport
* For minors, a parents’ passport is required
* Accommodation allotment letter issued by Central/State Govt. (not more than 3 years old)
* Certificate of Marriage issued by the Government containing address
* Bhamashah Card/Jan-Aadhaar card issued by Govt. of Rajasthan
* Certificate from Superintendent/Matron/Warden/Head of Institution of recognized shelter homes or orphanages, etc.
* Certificate of Address having photo issued by Municipal  
   Councillor
* Identity Card issued by recognized educational  
   institutions
* SSLC book containing photograph
* School Identity card
* School Transfer Certificate (TC)/School Leaving Certificate (SLC) containing name and address
* Extract of School Records containing name, address and photograph issued by Head of School
* Certificate of Identity containing name, address and photograph issued by Recognized Educational Institution signed by Head of Institute
* Certificate of identity containing name, DOB and photo issued by EPFO

## **List of Date of Birth Proofs – Documents Required for Aadhar Card**

The documents containing the date of birth proof of the applicant which will work for Aadhaar card registration are as follows:

* Certificate of birth
* SSLC Book/ Certificate
* Passport of the applicant
* PAN Card
* Certificate of Date of Birth which is issued by Group A Gazetted Officer on letterhead
* A certificate or ID Card having photo and DOB duly signed and issued by a Government authority
* Photo ID card having DOB, issued by recognized Educational Institution
* Marksheet which has been issued by any Government Board or University
* Government Photo Id Card or Photo Identity Proof or PSU issued ID card which contains DoB
* Pension Payment Order (Central or State)
* Central Government Health Service Scheme Photo Card or Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme Photo Identity card
* School Leaving Certificate (SLC)/ School Transfer Certificate (TC) having name and DOB
* Extract of School Records issued by Head of School containing name, DOB and photo
* Certificate of Identity containing name, date of birth and photograph issued by recognized Educational Institution signed by Head of Institute
* Certificate of identity containing name, DOB and photograph issued by EPFO

## **Proofs of Relationship – Documents Required for Aadhaar Enrollment**

The list of documents required for ascertaining the relationship of the applicant with the family’s head for Aadhaar card enrolment are as follows:

* PDS Card
* Job card of MNREGA
* Medical card issued by the State Government, CGHS, ECHS and also ESIC
* Canteen card of the Army
* Pension card
* Passport of the applicant
* Any family entitlement document issued by any Central or State Government
* Registrar of Birth/Municipal Corporation or any local government body issued Birth Certificate
* Government issued Marriage Certificate
* Address card having name and photo issued by Department of Posts
* Bhamashah Card/Jan-Aadhaar card issued by Govt. of Rajasthan
* Discharge slip/card issued by Government hospitals for birth of a child
* Certificate of Identity containing photo issued by MP/MLA/MLC/Municipal Councillor/Gazetted Officer
* Certificate of Identity containing photo and relationship with HoF issued by Village Panchayat Head/Mukhiya/its equivalent authority (for rural areas)

Any one document from each category is required to be enclosed with the form for the successful issuance of the Aadhaar card

## **Documents Required for Aadhar Card for Children**

The list of documents required for issuing Aadhaar cards for children is similar to that for a normal applicant. However, one of the parents has to provide their Aadhaar copy in addition to the documents required by normal applicants for obtaining a child’s Aadhaar card.

Also, children below 5 years do not have to submit their biometric data. It is only required when they attain 5 years of age. It is then when their biometric data is taken. The following are the documents required for [Aadhaar card for child](https://www.paisabazaar.com/aadhar-card/aadhar-card-for-children/) above 5 years:

* Proof of residence
* Proof of identity
* Birth certificate
* Aadhaar of any one of the parents

**The documents accepted as Identity proof are given below:**

* Passport Copy
* PAN Card Copy
* Voter ID Copy
* Driving License

**The documents accepted as Address proof are given below:**

* Passport Copy of Spouse
* A Copy of Ration Card
* Voter ID Card
* Driving License
* Credit Card Statement (last 3 months)
* Bank Statement Or Passbook
* Electricity Bill (Last 3 months)
* Water bill (Last 3 months)
* Gas Connection Bill (Last 3 months)
* Landline Phone Bill (Last 3 months)
* Insurance Policy

It has to be kept in mind that applying for a new Aadhaar card is purely voluntary on the part of the individual and not compulsory. Also, failing to submit all the requisite documents gives UIDAI the power to revoke the issuance of the Aadhaar card anytime they like.

### **Documents Required for OCI Cardholders/ LTV Document Holders/ Nepal & Bhutan Nationals and Other Resident Foreigners**

Given below is the list of acceptable documents required for Aadhaar Card for OCI cardholders/ LTV document holders/ Nepal & Bhutan nationals as well as other Resident Foreigners:

* **For OCI Cardholders:** Valid OCI card along with valid foreign passport for residents who have stayed in India at least 182 days in the last one year is acceptable as ID proof

* **For Long Term VISA (LTV) Document Holders:** Identity and address proof in the form of a valid Long Term VISA (LTV) document and  valid/expired foreign passport of origin country issued to minorities communities of Afghanistan, Pakistan and Bangladesh such as  Hindus, Buddhists, Jains,  Sikhs, Parsis and Christians

* **For Nepal and Bhutan Nationals:** (Any one of the identity proofs)
  + Passport of Nepal/ Bhutan for Nepal/ Bhutan nationals
  + In case passport is not available, any 2 of the following documents having the same address can be submitted:

1. 1. 1. Nepalese/ Bhutanese Citizenship Certificate
      2. Voter Identity Card issued by the Election Commission of Bhutan/Nepal
      3. Limited validity Photo Identity Certificate issued by Nepalese Mission/Royal Bhutanese Mission in India

* **Other Resident Foreigners:**
* Valid VISA and valid foreign passport of resident foreigners who have stayed in India for at least 182 days in the past one year is acceptable as an identity proof

or

* Valid Registration Certificate/ Residential permit issued by FRRO/FRO to the resident foreigners (except OCI card holders, LTV document holders and Nepal/ Bhutan nationals) is acceptable as an address proof

### **Aadhaar Card as a Document Proof**

Aadhaar card can be used as a proof of identity and proof of residence while applying for the following instruments:

* [Savings account](https://www.paisabazaar.com/savings-account/)
* [Credit cards](https://www.paisabazaar.com/credit-cards/)
* [Personal loans](https://www.paisabazaar.com/personal-loan/)
* [Home loans](https://www.paisabazaar.com/home-loan/)
* [Business loans](https://www.paisabazaar.com/business-loan/)
* [Fixed deposits](https://www.paisabazaar.com/fixed-deposit/)

It is worth noting that Aadhaar is not mandatory for these instruments as of now but it can be used as regular document proof. Aadhaar Card is issued to every person and different documents are required for Aadhaar Card for school students, employed citizens, etc.

## **FAQs on Documents Required for Aadhaar Card**

### **Q. What are the documents required for Aadhaar Card for NRIs?**

**Ans.**NRIs having a valid Indian passport (adult or child) are eligible to apply for an Aadhaar card. The following are the common documents required by UIDAI for this purpose:

* **Proof of Identity:**(Any one of) PAN Card/Ration Card/Voter ID/Passport/Driving License, etc.
* **Proof of Address:**(Any one of) Passport/Voter ID/Driving License/Ration Card/Utility Bill/Bank Passbook, etc.
* **Proof of Date of Birth:**(Any one of) Passport/Birth Certificate/PAN Card, etc.

**Also read: [Aadhaar Card for NRIs and Foreigners](https://www.paisabazaar.com/aadhar-card/aadhaar-card-for-non-resident-indian/)**

### **Q. Is it possible to get an Aadhaar card without any documents?**

**Ans.** In case you do not have any documents, you can apply for Aadhaar card through the Head of Family (HoF).

### **Q. What documents are needed for changing one’s surname on an Aadhaar card?**

**Ans.** You can furnish any of the following documents to change surname in Aadhaar card after marriage:

* Voter ID card
* Driving License
* PAN Card
* Marriage Certificate
* Passport

**Also Read : [Documents Required for PAN Card](https://www.paisabazaar.com/pan-card/documents-required-for-pan-card/)**

### **Q. What documents are needed for changing/updating address in Aadhaar card?**

**Ans.** [Documents needed for changing address in the Aadhaar card](https://www.paisabazaar.com/aadhar-card/aadhaar-card-update-correction/) are the same that are needed for proof of residence at the time of enrolment. You can use any one of the proofs to update your residential address in your Aadhaar card.

### **Q. Can I change Aadhar name without proof?**

**Ans.** It is not possible to change your name in Aadhaar without a valid identity proof. You will have to provide at least one scanned copy of proof of identity such as driving license, PAN card, etc.

### **Q. Can we get Aadhar without birth certificate?**

**Ans.** In case you don’t have a birth certificate, you can use the tehsildar’s letter or school leaving certificate as birth proof to get your Aadhaar card.

### **Q. What documents are required for Aadhar card biometric update?**

**Ans.** No documents are required to update your documents in Aadhaar.

It is very important to keep your Aadhaar details updated in order to avoid issues while accessing banking, government, telecom, and other essential services. Whether you need to change your address, mobile number, date of birth, or biometric information, UIDAI provides both online and offline methods for Aadhaar correction and updates. In this guide, you will learn how to update and correct your Aadhaar details easily using both methods.

### Free Aadhaar Card Update or Correction Details

**[UIDAI](https://www.bankbazaar.com/aadhar-card/uidai.html) (Unique Identification Authority of India) has announced that [Aadhaar card](https://www.bankbazaar.com/aadhar-card.html)**holders can update their identity and address documents online free of cost till 14 June 2027.

## Aadhaar Update Categories

Aadhaar details can mainly be updated under two categories, which are as given below:

Follow the process given below to update the name, address, gender, and date of birth details online:

Step 1: Go to the official MyAadhaar portal and click on ‘Login’.

Step 2: You must enter a 12-digit Aadhaar number and Captcha code for authentication.

Step 3: You will receive an OTP on your registered mobile number.

Step 5: Enter the updated information and upload the required documents.

## How to Update Aadhaar Address using HoF Consent

In case a person does not have any address proof in their name, the following steps must be followed for updating the Aadhar address:

Step 1: Visit the official MyAadhaar portal and select the option for HoF-based address update.

Step 2: The Aadhaar number of the Head of Family is entered for verification.

Step 3: After successful verification, you must upload a Proof of Relationship document.

Step 4: The address update fee of Rs.75 is paid.

Step 5: After payment, the system generates a Service Request Number (SRN).

Step 6: An SMS notification is sent to the Head of Family for consent.

Step 7: The Head of Family must log in to the My Aadhaar portal and provide consent within 30 days.

Step 8: Once the consent is approved, the address in the Aadhaar is updated.

## How to Update Mobile Number in Aadhaar Card Online

UIDAI has introduced a convenient feature that allows Aadhaar holders to update their mobile number through the Aadhaar app. Here are the steps given below:

Step 1: Download the [new ‘Aadhaar’ app](https://www.bankbazaar.com/aadhar-card/new-aadhaar-app-with-face-id-qr-code.html) from the [Play Store or App Store](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=in.gov.uidai.pehchaan).

Step 3: The app will prompt you to send an SMS for mobile number verification.

Step 4: Face Authentication is completed, and a 6-digit PIN is set.

Step 5: Click on ‘Services’ and select the ‘Mobile Number Update’ option.

Step 6: The mobile number is entered, and the OTP is filled in.

Step 7: Enter your new mobile number and the corresponding OTP.

Step 8: Face authentication is completed, and a fee of Rs.75 is paid to finish the update.

From 1 November 2025, users can update Aadhaar information such as name, address, and mobile number online through the myAadhaar portal. All Aadhaar holders need to keep their details updated to avoid service restrictions and potential financial issues.

The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) will launch the e-Aadhaar mobile app this month. This new app will help users in updating their address, Date of Birth, and mobile number directly from their smartphones. Users can also upload documents such as a PAN, passport, or driving licence for proof. However, biometric updates like fingerprints or iris scans will still need to be done at Aadhaar centres. Aadhaar biometrics can now be updated for free for a year for children aged 5 to 17, according to the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI). Beginning on 1st October and continuing until 30th September 2026, the new Aadhaar upgrade will benefit around 6 crore children globally. It used to cost parents Rs. 125 for each biometric update if the change was made outside of the specified age range. For children in this age group, all Aadhaar biometric updates will now be free for a year, regardless of when they are released. Aadhaar numbers may be temporarily blocked if biometrics are not updated on time. This could affect Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) programs, entrance exams, scholarships, and school admissions. You can finish the biometric update procedure at any approved enrollment facility or Aadhaar Seva Kendra (ASK) by making an online appointment via the UIDAI website or mAadhaar app.

### Aadhaar Fee Structure Update

The new fee structure announced by the UIDAI for Aadhaar services will take effect from 1 October 2025. According to the new fee structure, the charges for major Aadhaar-related services have increased. Aadhaar services previously costing Rs.50 and Rs.75 will now cost Rs.75 and Rs.100. Starting from 2028, the Rs.75 and Rs.125 services will be increased to Rs.90 and Rs.150, respectively.

However, biometric updates for children aged 5 to 7 and teenagers aged 15 to 17 years are still free. For children aged 7 to 15, biometric updates are free until 30 September 2026. The charge for other biometric updates will be Rs.125. Demographic updates, such as name, address, gender, and DOB, are also free when done along with biometric updates. Standalone demographic updates cost between Rs.50 and Rs.70. Updating identity and address documents using the myAadhaar portal is free until 14 June 2026, and updating through Aadhaar centres costs Rs.50 to Rs.70. The charge for home enrolment services is Rs.700, plus the standard update fees.

### UIDAI Reminder: Update Biometric Details of Children After Age 5 and 15

The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) states that biometric updates are required once a child turns five. Since fingerprints and iris scans are not developed at that age, the card depends only on a photo, name, and address. The Aadhaar card is called Baal Aadhaar, printed in blue, and is issued for children under the age of five. According to reports, approximately 17 crore Aadhaar updates for children are still pending in India. If a biometric update is missing, parents must pay a fee (currently Rs.100).

Instead of providing photocopies, Aadhaar holders will be able to electronically disclose their identities in the upcoming weeks. According to a TOI article, users would be able to share a full version of the document through QR code using a new mobile app from the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI). A system that allows users to alter their name, date of birth, address, and phone number from the comfort of their own homes will be introduced by UIDAI. By November, providing fingerprints and iris scans at an enrollment center will be the only in-person step. The goal of the action is to reduce paperwork, reduce the possibility of fake documents, and speed up the procedure for citizens. Birth certificates, driver's licenses, passports, PANs, PDSs, and MNREGA are among the documents from which UIDAI obtains its data directly. The QR-code approach is ready to be used for identity verification on trains, hotel check-ins, and property deals.

### Aadhaar Revamp 2025

The UIDAI (Unique Identification Authority of India) has announced an Aadhaar revamp to introduce major changes. The changes include launching a QR code-based application that eliminates the need to submit physical photocopies of Aadhaar cards. It enables cardholders to share digital copies of Aadhaar in complete or masked formats. By November 2025, UIDAI is prepared to automate Aadhaar updates except for biometric details, through integrating official databases. This aims to make Aadhaar updating easier and more convenient for users by removing the need to visit Aadhaar centres.

### Aadhaar Updates Can Be Done Online for Free, Until 14 June 2026

The announcement by UIDAI indicates that Aadhaar holders can upload their documents for verification free of cost on the myAadhaar portal until 14 June 2026. The aim is to correct any Aadhaar record inaccuracies, especially for those whose Aadhaar is more than 10 years old or who have recently changed information. It is important to understand that biometric, email, and telephone number changes must be made at an Aadhaar center and are subject to regular fees.

### Aadhaar-Based Facial Recognition to Fully Replace Biometric Attendance in Medical Colleges

The National Medical Commission (NMC) has announced that the biometric attendance system will be discontinued and fully replaced by an Aadhaar-based facial recognition method from 1 May 2025. The rule will apply to all medical college faculty members across India in which teachers give their attendance by using a special face scan app that is linked to their Aadhaar number. The app can be downloaded from both Play Store and App Store. This change has been made to stop the issue of "ghost faculty", i.e., teachers who are listed on college records but do not actually work there. All the medical colleges have been asked to make sure every teacher is ready to use the new system before the deadline.

### Linking Aadhaar numbers with electoral roll data has been mandated by the Election Commission of India

As per a recent circular from the Election Commission of India (ECI), officials have been instructed to link Aadhaar numbers with electoral roll data. This directive, sent to all Chief Electoral Officers (CEOs) in states and Union Territories, mandates the integration of voter roll data with Aadhaar and mobile numbers to enhance the accuracy of voter identification. This initiative is expected to prevent cases of a single voter possessing multiple Elector Photo Identity Card (EPIC) numbers.

### Aadhaar Good Governance Portal launched in India

India has revamped its Aadhaar Good Governance Portal by adding a new feature that allows citizens to directly report on the performance of public services using their Aadhaar credentials. With this improvement, users can register grievances, track resolution status, and review government efficiency via an enhanced, user-friendly interface. This initiative is intended to boost the transparency, accountability, and overall responsiveness of public services.

### Linking Aadhaar with UAN mandatory by 15 January 2025 to secure ELI scheme benefits

The EPFO has urged employees to activate their UAN and link it with Aadhaar and their bank account by January 15 to remain eligible for the Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) scheme. Aadhaar should also be connected to a mobile number to enable EPF fund transfers directly to the bank account. UAN activation ensures access to EPFO services like online EPF withdrawals and balance checks. Missing the deadline may lead to ineligibility for ELI scheme benefits.

  Changes in life events such as marriage may lead to Aadhaar number holders changing their basic demographic details such as name and address. Address and mobile number could also change due to migration to newer locations. Aadhaar number holders may also want changes in their relative’s details due to changes in life events such marriage, death of a relative etc. In addition, Aadhaar number holders could have other personal reasons to change their mobile number, email address etc.
* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  Changes in various service delivery platforms may lead Aadhaar number holders to declaration request changes and to add mobile number to CIDR etc.
* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  Errors made during the enrolment process wherein the demographic data of individuals seeking to enrol may have been captured incorrectly.Changes to “DoB/Age” and “Gender” fields are expected primarily due to enrolment errors.
* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  Since an individual can enrol anywhere in India, it may happen that a native speaker of language "A" is enrolled by an operator of language "B" and consequently the individual’s local language of enrolment is "B". Later, the Aadhaar number holder may want to change the local language of enrolment to another that he/she prefers. If so, then all the demographic information that is printed on the Aadhaar letter will need to be updated in the new local language.
* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  UIDAI may also ascertain availability of POI, POA and other documents collected at the time of enrolment/update and its quality and decide to notify Aadhaar number holder to update their demographic information and submit the required document.

Biometric update, the need could arise from:

* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  **Age <5 years at the time of initial enrolment** -The child should be re-enroled when the child attains an age of 5 years and all biometric data should be provided. A de-duplication would be done for the child at this stage. This request will be treated similar to a new enrolment request while retaining the original Aadhaar number
* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  **Age between 5 and 15 years at the time of enrolment** -  The Aadhaar number holder should furnish all biometrics for updates when he/she attains age of 15 years.
* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  **Age >15 years at the time of enrolment** – Aadhaar number holders are recommended to update their biometric data every 10 years.
* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  Events like accidents or diseases leading to biometric exception
* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  As the Aadhaar authentication service is becoming ubiquitous, Aadhaar number holders may also approach for biometric updates because of authentication failures (called false rejects – where a correct Aadhaar number holder with valid Aadhaar number may be incorrectly rejected) which may result from incorrect biometric capture or poor biometric quality captured at the time of enrolment. With improvements in technology, it may be possible to capture better quality biometrics in the CIDR.
* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  UIDAI may verify the **quality** of biometrics captured during enrolment/ update and decide a threshold quality. All Aadhaar number holders with biometrics below the threshold level would/**will** be notified by UIDAI to update their biometrics

Aadhaar details that can be updated are:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Demographic Information | Name, Address, Date of Birth/Age, Gender, Mobile Number, Email Address, Relationship Status and Information Sharing Consent |
| Biometric Information | Iris, Finger Prints and Facial Photograph |

UIDAI update process accepts wide range of PoI (Proof of Identity) and PoA (Proof of Address) documents. View the [List of supporting documents](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-05/List_of_Supporting_Document_for_Aadhaar_Enrolment_and_Update.pdf) **Doc Type: PDF SIze: 1.6MB.**

Modes of Update

1. Via Online

The online mode offers address update to the Aadhaar number holders where the Aadhaar number holder can directly place the address update request on the myAadhaar portal. The Aadhaar number holder needs to have mobile number registered with Aadhaar for using this  service. The Aadhaar number is required to login to the [portal](https://myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in/) by the Aadhaar number holder. The Aadhaar number holder is authenticated using sent OTP on his/her registered mobile number. To complete the update process, Aadhaar number holder needs to upload the [supporting POA documents](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-05/List_of_Supporting_Document_for_Aadhaar_Enrolment_and_Update.pdf) **Doc Type: PDF Size: 1.6MB** , which will be verified against requested data at a later stage by a quality and processing team.

By Visiting Aadhaar Enrolment Centre

Aadhaar number holders place the demographic/biometric update request with the help of an operator at an [Aadhaar Enrolment Centre](https://appointments.uidai.gov.in/easearch.aspx). In such a case, the documentary evidence is collected by the operator at the time of accepting the request. The document verification by the verifier also happens at the time of placing the update request. UIDAI currently has envisaged three modes for Assisted Updates:

a. Update Client Standard

* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  **Fields**: All biometric and demographic fields as well as local language can be updated
* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  **Identity Authentication**: Biometric check at the back-end.

Document Verification

* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  Verification done for those fields which require documentary evidence.
* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  Verification done by verifier appointed by UIDAI/Registrars present at Enrolment / Update Centre.

Form Filling and Acknowledgement

* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  Done by the operator on update client as requested by the Aadhaar number holder. Handles spelling, language issues, transliteration, etc. Operator will provide biometric sign off against every update request.

Aadhaar number holder gets an acknowledgement receipt with Update Request Number (URN) which can be tracked.

![Card image](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-05/update_client_standard.webp)

b. Update Client Lite (UCL)

* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  **Fields**: All demographic fields and Photo as well as local language can be updated.
* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  **Identity Authentication**: Biometric Authentication of Aadhaar number holder.

Document Verification

* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  Verification done for those fields which require documentary evidence
* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  Verification done by verifier appointed by UIDAI/Registrars present at Aadhaar Enrolment / Update Centre.
* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  The verification procedure followed should be in line with DDSVP Committee Recommendations followed during enrolment process

Form Filling in software and Acknowledgement

* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  Done by the operator on update client as requested by the Aadhaar number holder. Aadhaar number holder gets an acknowledgement receipt with Enrolment ID (EID) which can be used for checking status. Operator will provide biometric sign off against every update request.

## How to update address on Aadhaar card?

If you have recently moved to a new city or changed your address, now you can update your new address even online. Any resident with a registered mobile number can update their profile using Aadhaar self-service Portal.

Registered mobile number is mandatory to receive a one time password for login. First, you need to log in to the portal. You can update your address by following Option A or B:

To update your address online, make sure you have original scanned images of supporting documents. The list of valid address proof includes passport, voter id, ration card or telephone bill that shouldn’t be older than three months etc.

## How to update mobile number and name on Aadhaar card?

Only address of the Aadhaar holder can be corrected/updated online. You can search for the nearest enrolment centre by clicking on “Locate Enrolment Center” on uidai.gov.in.

# Process to Know How NRIs Can Apply for Aadhaar Card

[Manoj Sodhani](https://www.services2nri.com/blog/author/s2nriusername/)  [NRI NEWS](https://www.services2nri.com/blog/category/nri-news/)

The question arises whether NRIs can apply for Aadhaar card in India. The answer is yes, NRIs are eligible to apply for an Aadhaar card in India. However, there are certain conditions that need to be fulfilled by NRIs in order to apply for this card.

**What is Aadhaar Card?**

An **[Aa](https://www.services2nri.com/blog/must-aadhaar-card-passport-bank-account/)**[**dhaar card is a unique identification number**](https://www.services2nri.com/blog/must-aadhaar-card-passport-bank-account/) issued by the Indian government. These 12-digit numbers serve as a unique identifier for an individual, including non-resident Indians (NRIs) and Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs) residing abroad. This nationality identification card is a significant document for various government schemes and services. Also, you can use it for private transactions such as opening a bank account, obtaining a mobile phone connection, and so on. Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) may also apply for this card in India, subject to certain conditions.

**Who Issues It?**

The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), a statutory authority established by the Indian government has the right to issue it. This very same authority has made it possible for non-residents to apply for an Aadhaar card in India. It can be easily done through a process known as the “enrollment process”. The enrollment process requires applicants to provide personal details and biometric information such as fingerprints, iris scans, and photographs, and finally, these details are submitted to the UIDAI.

**Residential Condition**

Indian migrants need to be present in India at the time of the application process. It means that they cannot apply for an Aadhaar card online or through any other means from outside India. They must physically be present in India to apply for the card.

**Eligibility for Aadhaar Card**

NRIs who wish to apply for an Aadhaar card in India must meet certain eligibility criteria.

As aforesaid, they must have been residing in India for a period of at least 182 days (6 months) in the 12 months preceding the date of application. This means that non-residents who have been living abroad for an extended period of time may not be eligible to apply for an Aadhaar card in India.

**Required Documents**

These emigrants must visit an Aadhaar enrollment center, which can be found in various locations across the country. At the enrollment center, they must provide these documents:

* Proof of identity and proof of address, as well as their biometric information
* Proof of identity can be provided through documents such as a passport, PAN card, driving license, or voter ID card
* Enclose proof of address, which can be provided through documents such as a bank statement, utility bill, or rental agreement
* Attach their mobile number and email address, which will be used to communicate with them about this identification card

**Verification**

Once the enrollment process is complete, the competent authority will verify the information provided by the emigrants and issue an Aadhaar card if everything is fine or in order.

**Processing**

This identification card will be sent to the NRI’s address within a few weeks of the enrollment process. In the meantime, they can check or track the status of this card by visiting the UIDAI website and entering their enrollment ID and other details.

**Process to Get Aadhaar Card**

Formally, you (as NRI) can follow these steps to get it quickly. Once these conditions are met, you can apply for an Aadhaar card by following the below steps:

**Step 1:** Find the Nearest Enrollment Center

You can find the nearest enrollment center on the aforementioned [**website**](https://uidai.gov.in/) , or by calling the toll-free number 1947. You can also book an appointment online for the enrollment process.

**Step 2:** Fill Out the Enrollment Form

You need to fill out the Aadhaar enrollment form at the center. The form requires personal information such as name, date of birth, address, and contact details.

**Step 3:** Submit Identity and Address Proof

You need to submit proof of identity and address, along with a copy of your passport.

**Step 4:** Provide Biometric Data

NRIs need to provide their biometric data by undergoing a fingerprint scan, iris scan, and photograph.

**Step 5:** Receive Acknowledgement Slip

Once the enrollment process is complete, you will receive an acknowledgement slip. The slip contains an enrollment ID, which can be used to check the status of this card.

**Step 6:** Receive Aadhaar card

Emigrants will receive their Aadhaar card via post at the address provided in the enrollment form.

It is important to note that NRIs who apply for this card in India are subject to the same rules and regulations as Indian citizens. This means that you must use your card for legitimate purposes only. Also, you must not use it for any illegal or fraudulent activities. Additionally, keeping your card safe and secure is a must, and you should not share your Aadhaar number or other details with anyone except for authorised agencies or individuals.

# Aadhaar Enrolment

Learn about the Aadhaar enrolment process, required documents, biometric capture and enrolment options available across India free of cost.

Process

The Aadhaar enrolment process includes visiting Enrolment Centre, filling the enrolment form, getting demographic and biometric data captured, submitting proof of Identity and address documents, before collecting acknowledgement slip containing Enrolment ID. The highlights of Aadhaar enrolment are:

* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  Aadhaar enrolment is free of cost.
* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  You can go to any authorized [Aadhaar enrolment centre](https://bookappointment.uidai.gov.in/) anywhere in India with your proof of identity and proof of address documents
* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  UIDAI process accepts **wide range of PoI (Proof of Identity) and PoA (Proof of Address) documents. Document:- PDF Size:-1.6 M** View the [list of supporting documents](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-05/List_of_Supporting_Document_for_Aadhaar_Enrolment_and_Update.pdf). Common proofs of identity and address are election photo ID card, Ration card, passport and driving license.
* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  Photo ID cards like Voter Card and Govt ID cards are permissible for identity proof. Address proof documents also include water - electricity - Landline telephone bills for the last three months.
* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  Certificate of Address having photo issued by MP or MLA /Gazetted Officer/Tehsildar on letterhead or by Village Panchayat head or its equivalent authority (for rural areas) is accepted as valid PoA. Even if someone in a family does not have individual valid documents, the the individual seeking to enrol can still enrol if his/her name exists in family entitlement document. In this case the **Head of Family** mentioned in entitlement document needs to be enrolled first with valid PoI & PoA document. The head of the Family can then introduce other members in the family while they are enrolling. UIDAI accepts many document types as Proof of Relationship. Please [View the list of supporting documents. Document:- PDF Size:-1.6 MB](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-05/List_of_Supporting_Document_for_Aadhaar_Enrolment_and_Update.pdf).

**To summarise, there are two approaches for enrolment:**

**Document Based**

Submission of one valid Proof of Identity (PoI) document and one valid Proof of Address(PoA) document

**Head Of Family (Hof)-based**

Head of family (HoF) may introduce family members by means of documents, which establish the Proof of Relationship (PoR).

![Card image](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-05/capturing_demographic_and_biometric_1.webp)

* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  You need to enrol only once, as multiple enrolments will result in rejections unless it is advised by UIDAI.
* ![arrow](/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

  The waiting time for Aadhaar is 180 days after receipt of **enrolment** data packets in CIDR.

Where to Enrol

Enrolment in all the states/UTs is being covered by UIDAI. **Individuals** of all states/UTs **seeking enrolment**, are required to enrol **only at** nearby [Aadhaar Enrolment Centre/Aadhaar Camps](https://bookappointment.uidai.gov.in/).
